keyRules: In the open category, the maximum height is 120 m, measured as the distance to the closest point on the Earth's surface — not simply straight down, so near a slope the ground beside you can also count. Within 50 m of a tall artificial obstacle (over 105 m), the entity responsible for the obstacle can request permission to fly up to 15 m above the height of the obstacle.

You must register as a drone operator if your drone weighs 250 g or more (or could transfer more than 80 J of kinetic energy on impact) — this also applies to toys. Below 250 g, registration is still required if the drone has a sensor capable of capturing personal data, unless it is considered a toy under the EU Toy Safety Directive. Pilot training/certificate requirements are regulated separately and depend on the drone's class and subcategory.

In Switzerland, the minimum age for remote pilots is 12 years in the «open» operating category and 14 years in the «specific» category (Art. 26 VLK, SR 748.941) — regardless of the drone's weight. Younger pilots may only fly under the direct supervision of a remote pilot who meets the requirements. When registering, children under 16 must name a legal representative. The A1/A3 proof of competency is obtained online and is valid for 5 years.
Mandatory liability insurance for drones weighing 250 g or more (coverage of CHF 1 million)
Members of model aircraft clubs: additional privileges under FOCA regulations

In the open category, you must keep the drone within your own line of sight, with the naked eye (glasses/contact lenses are fine; binoculars or a screen do not count) — or fly with the support of an observer, with clear and effective communication between you at all times so that you can jointly watch the airspace and avoid collisions. Follow-me mode is a separate exception, allowed up to 50 m from the pilot.
Do not fly over assemblies of people. Rules for uninvolved persons depend on subcategory, class mark and operating conditions; check the official matrix.

For drones over 250 g, operation is prohibited at a distance of less than 5 km from the runways of a civil or military aerodrome, and in an active CTR if a height of 120 m above ground is exceeded (Art. 28 VLK). The aerodrome management can define a reduced zone within the 5 km; exceptions are granted by the aerodrome management or the air traffic control unit.

Regardless of weight, operation is prohibited, among other places, over correctional facilities, over military areas as listed in the VLK annex, over outdoor switchgear of grid level 2, and within 750 m of nuclear power plants and the Würenlingen interim storage facility (Art. 27 VLK).
National Parks: Drone Use Restricted or Prohibited
Mountain regions: Be aware of helicopter flight paths (rescue, sightseeing flights)
importantNotes: Registration costs only CHF 10—a one-time fee with unlimited validity and no renewal required.

U-Space Zurich: Switzerland's first U-Space airspace is being introduced in the Zurich CTR (approx. 10 km × 17 km); use of U-Space services will be mandatory for all drone pilots in the area from the end of 2026 (one-time registration with a USSP required). Exempt: drones under 250 g, model aircraft, state flights. Legal basis: Art. 29a–29e VLK.
Mandatory Insurance for Drones Weighing 250 g or More (Coverage: CHF 1 Million)
Switzerland is not a member of the EU, but complies with EASA regulations through a bilateral agreement
Alpine helicopter routes are common—always keep an eye on the airspace
The DSG (Swiss Data Protection Act) applies when photographing identifiable individuals
